harbor-body.purpose: Light-theme descriptions, explanations and editorial prose.

harbor-chip-ink.purpose: Light-theme text carried by Shell Quiet chips.

current-mist.purpose: Dark-theme metadata and utility text on navy surfaces.

moon-current.purpose: Dark-theme descriptions, explanations and editorial prose.

moon-chip-ink.purpose: Dark-theme text carried by Midnight Surface Strong chips.

error.purpose: Failure state. Not emphasis, so it does not touch the Beacon Rule's claim on blue.
error.contrast: 5.24:1 on white, 5.68:1 on the dark surface

display.purpose: Held in reserve; nothing currently uses it.

sectionTitle.purpose: Headings that open a section within a page, delivered through --type-section-title.

subhead.purpose: The step between a section title and a card title: the hero issue number, the Editor's Pick title, and headings nested inside a card. Delivered through --type-subhead.

cardTitle.purpose: Card titles, app names, and the name of a category or collection. Delivered through --type-card-title.

tileTitle.purpose: Titles on the Explore taxonomy tiles, where a card title would wrap. Delivered through --type-tile-title.

dek.purpose: The standfirst under a page or section title, delivered through --type-dek; always one step above body.

metadata.purpose: Counts, sources, and secondary operational information.

controlLabel.purpose: The text on something you press. The only small role that is neither tracked nor uppercase, because a control is read as a word.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, small UI labels, and control legends.

mono.purpose: Data a reader might copy. Today that is the RSS feed URL and nothing else; it is not a costume for looking technical.

_contract.rule: A role is a family, a size, a weight and a line box, defined together.
_contract.fluidRolesExempt: Page Title, Section Title and Subhead set size with clamp(), so no single leading puts them on a step across the range.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs lifting off a scrimmed page: search, the navigation menu, the subscribe dialog.

shadows.name: night-modal
shadows.purpose: The same dialogs in the dark theme.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default state transitions for buttons, links, and cards.

motion.name: ease-quick
motion.purpose: Fast highlight changes such as search-result and micro-state feedback.

motion.name: ease-emphasis
motion.purpose: Longer opacity and visibility transitions used by hero-aware header states.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Card hover elevation and border changes; an exponential ease-out that settles instead of snapping.

motion.name: ease-arrive
motion.purpose: The site-wide scroll reveal: content fades in once, as the reader reaches it.

motion.name: ease-drift
motion.purpose: The Editor's Pick wash drifting across the hero card; paused off screen.

motion.name: ease-gleam
motion.purpose: The Editor's Pick edge gleam; paused off screen.

motion.name: swell
motion.purpose: The hero and divider wave bands breathing. Ambient, never travelling.

spacingMeta.rule: Structural vertical spacing is a whole multiple of --base (8px). The horizontal field grid is a separate system and does not divide by it.
spacingMeta.derived: --space-1..9 are calc(var(--base) * n); --eyebrow-gap is var(--space-1). Changing --base moves the whole scale. Structural vertical margin, padding and row-gap consumers use these tokens; horizontal field gutters remain independent.
spacingMeta.fluidExceptions: Horizontal only: the shell gutter, the homepage hero and app-detail rail column gaps, and the app icon frame that scales with its page. Fluid display type is exempt under The Line Box Rule.
spacingMeta.overlayException: Viewport-fitting search/RSS top offsets use min(9vh/10vh, 12 base units); mobile overlays respect safe-area insets. Page structural spacing remains stepped.
spacingMeta.searchResultInset: 16px horizontal field gutter; aligns hover/focus fills with the result-count inset

spans.filterAndSortPair: 4 tracks = one card span at every multi-column width

fieldAligned: directory toolbar incl. search field and Filter panel
gridMeta.wasSixFixedFields: Until 2026-09-07. Correct at the 1160px maximum only; controls held 180px literals and stopped matching cards below it.

sanctionedDecorativeAccent: archive terminus (second use of The Struck Light Rule)

variantMeta.rule: A component variant carries its base class as well as its own, so it outranks the base by specificity rather than by source order.

editorsPick.title: Subhead, not Card Title
editorsPick.contentOrder: identity, description, why it was chosen, Best For, tags
editorsPick.layout: single column in document order; flex, not grid

variantMeta.wasBroken: Until 2026-09-07 the base .app-card sat later in the file and won every shared property: declared grid rendered flex, declared fluid padding rendered 24px, declared Subhead rendered Card Title.

namedException.why: A page with no grid to fill has nothing to span, so rules and headings sit with the text. At 624px the line runs ~73 characters.

geometryMeta.pick: --pick-inset: var(--space-4); padding and radius share it, rim adds --pick-rim
geometryMeta.iconFrame: border-radius: 25%; shared by card (48px), hero (56px) and fluid detail (56-80px)
geometryMeta.filterPanel: --radius-md at all widths; mobile spans the page shell, not the viewport

exceptions: programmatically focused mobile navigation dialog container
focusMeta.standaloneAction: Accent at rest, accent-hover on interaction, no underline; shared focus ring

componentExampleMeta.authority: Current Astro components and styles govern implementation. Inspect the production routes listed in docs/COMPONENT_REFERENCE.md.
componentExampleMeta.panelBehaviour: An empty components array omits preview tiles; tokens and narrative remain available.
componentExampleMeta.futurePreviews: Render production components with their production styles; do not restore independent ds-* CSS.

headerInteractionMeta.hover: accent colour only; no theme-toggle rotation

narrative.overview:
App Waypoint feels like a calm dock under overcast light: cool paper, deep-water text, and a single reliable blue used sparingly so the page never shouts. It is editorial rather than promotional, organized like a magazine, but laid out like a utility. Dense information sits inside soft cards and quiet section breaks instead of loud banners.

The language prefers stable geometry, soft depth, and generous breathing room. Serif headlines carry the authority; the system sans supports the utility layers, controls, and metadata. The result is familiar and trustworthy, with enough atmosphere to feel considered but not styled for its own sake.
keyCharacteristics: White paper on a cool fog-grey field, with navy ink.
Beacon blue reserved for actions and current states.
Corners derived from component insets and nested geometry, with proportional app icon frames.
Dense content organized through cards, chips, and careful spacing.

rules.name: The Fog Rule
rules.body: Every light-mode neutral sits on Deep Sea's hue — OKLCH hue 253–258, the ink's own axis — at a chroma of 0.010 or less: Surf Foam 0.000, Drift Mist 0.005, Harbor Fog 0.008, Shell Strong 0.010. That is what keeps the field reading as harbor weather rather than default UI grey. A neutral off that axis, or any warm tone reintroduced into the light theme, breaks the day palette.

rules.name: The Beacon Rule
rules.body: Blue is reserved for actions, links, focus, and active states. It should not become page chrome or decorative noise.

rules.name: The Surface Ink Rule
rules.body: Primary reading copy, chip text and metadata are separate semantic roles: --body-text, --chip-text and --muted. Each theme maps them onto the surface's blue axis. Descriptions and editorial prose use --body-text; tag labels use --chip-text; dates, counts, breadcrumbs, sources and operational hints use --muted. Every mapping clears AA on its supported surfaces.

rules.name: The No Content Divider Rule
rules.body: Content is separated by spacing, not rules. Structural vertical spacing derives from --base through --space-1..9; named section/hero/footer tokens step at the responsive breakpoints. Control boundaries are not content dividers.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose uses --measure (52ch), following its own font and size. About is the named exception: --about-measure (624px) applies to title, dek, headings and prose.

rules.name: The One Page Title Rule
rules.body: Every page opens with its title in Headline at --type-page-title, hard against --page-start-space with no margin of its own, and the dek 16px beneath at --type-dek. App detail pages are not an exception; presence comes from composition, never from a private type scale.

rules.name: The Serif-Utility Split
rules.body: Serif type carries the editorial voice; the system sans carries the operational voice. Mixing them casually weakens both jobs.

rules.name: The Soft Hull Rule
rules.body: Surfaces lift with a soft shadow and a border change, not with hard edges or dramatic offsets.

rules.name: The One Hover Rule
rules.body: Every card that leads somewhere shares one hover contract: rest at Ambient Card, move to Hover Lift and a border of color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 42%, var(--line)), cross over 320ms on cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), under (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) only. Container cards that hold their own links stay flat, and the explore carousel suppresses the lift because its stack already carries depth.

rules.name: Control heights follow the grid
rules.body:
Control dimensions use whole multiples of the 8px
base, with roles defined by the actual component. Both `.button` and `.button.secondary`
have a 48px minimum height with horizontal padding of 24px and no vertical padding. Header controls,
directory toolbar controls and collection badge rows are also 48px. Sort menu options
are 40px, rising to 48px on coarse pointers. Tags, active-filter chips, category rows,
filter options and reset controls use 32px; filter options and reset controls rise to
48px on coarse pointers. Mobile directory search and sort controls use 56px. Active-filter
chips retain their visible height and expand their hit area through a pseudo-element.
Standalone small targets have a 24px floor; links inside sentences remain inline.

Primary buttons use an accent border and label; secondary buttons use neutral ones.
Both are transparent at rest. On hover or keyboard focus, the primary gains a 10% accent
tint and both inherit a 1px lift; the secondary stays transparent. Reduced motion removes
the lift. These are existing button exceptions to the general colour-only hover rule.

Historical: this was called *The Two Control Heights* until 2026-09-06 and described
44px primary / 38px secondary controls. That pair is superseded by the component roles
above; it is not a recipe for new controls.

rules.name: The Plain Dash Rule
rules.body: Public editorial copy uses no em dash and no en dash. Restructure to a period, a comma, a colon, or parentheses, and set number and date ranges with a plain hyphen. Outside the rule: page-title separators, which are an indexed SEO and publishing convention; quoted external titles in source notes and reading lists, where changing the punctuation misquotes the source; and code comments, which no reader sees. The rule covers the site's public copy, not the repository's own documentation. The vendored taste-skill states a blanket ban covering titles too; this narrower rule governs here and that skill is left unedited so it stays diffable against upstream.

rules.name: The Struck Light Rule
rules.body: The Editor's Pick card in the hero is lit by the featured app's own colour, and that light moves: a wide wash drifting across the card over 28s and a gleam travelling its edge over 11s, both on pseudo-elements of that one card. It is reserved for the one app an issue argues for. The colour is normalised, never raw: icon hues across picks run from saturated magenta to near-black, so scripts/extract-icon-accent.mjs fixes every pick to one lightness and chroma in OKLCh and commits the result to the app record as iconAccent. The Beacon Rule survives because the colour is light on one card and never reaches a link, control or state. A pick with no usable icon has no iconAccent and renders the ordinary card. The wash sits on its own layer at negative z-index rather than in the card background, because the shared hover contract sets the background shorthand and an intermediate custom property stops the drift resolving. Both loops pause off screen and stop under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Binding Rule
rules.body: --eyebrow-gap derives from --space-1 (8px) and binds each label to its content. --space-3 (24px) separates labelled groups.

rules.name: The One Card Height Rule
rules.body: Every app card on a page is the same height and their regions line up across the whole grid, not just within a row. The grid defines three repeating tracks and each card spans them as a subgrid. Floors are what the tallest record actually needs, measured across all 102: 230/149/122 at the narrowest three-column width, 205/99/88 above 1100px. The first and last include the card's 24px padding, since a subgrid item's padding comes out of the tracks it spans. minmax rather than fixed, so a longer future record makes its own band taller instead of clipping. This replaced per-region min-height budgets, which any card that overflowed one, usually a second line of tags, pushed out of step with its row. Reading cards are the exception and align on their own terms: they carry .app-card but hold three parts inside a wrapper, so card and wrapper both subgrid onto the shared rows, and they take no floors so a card is as tall as the longest of the three and no taller. The floors apply only where the grid is multi-column: below 921px each card is its own height, because a single column has no neighbour to agree with and the budgets, sized for a 270px card, added a median 159px per card and 17,000px of scrolling on a phone.

rules.name: The Carousel Stack Rule
rules.body: The explore carousel's centre card is the same object as a directory card, 376x424, and the track's height follows it rather than being a number of its own. A flanking card sits between the page and the centre so it reads as set back: dark at luminance 21 between 18 and 26, light at 246 between 236 and 255. Light carries no dimming filter, its palette being near-neutral by design, so brightness only drags toward grey. Desaturation belongs to the app icon, not the card: saturate() on the slot drains the card's surface too and turned a 63% navy into a 16% grey. Opacity is binary, 0 off stage and 1 on it, with the fade on the card's contents, because a slot fading up while its z-index has already jumped to the front lets the outgoing card show through the incoming one. Only the centre carries --carousel-drag, in the responsive overrides as well as the base rule. Icons are primed in a window of -2 to +2, because every off-stage slot is hidden and stacked and a lazy icon has no reason to fetch until its card arrives.

rules.name: The One Scrim Rule
rules.body: Search, the navigation menu and the subscribe dialog share one backdrop token, --scrim, and it follows the theme. All three were a near-black navy in both themes, which is right over a dark page and turns a light one grey; light takes Harbor Fog at 62% so the page stays bright and the blur does the obscuring. Blur is identical across the three at blur(12px) saturate(110%). A panel separates from the scrim on its own shadow, not on the scrim being dark.

rules.name: The Target Floor Rule
rules.body: Standalone small targets have a 24px floor; links inside sentences remain inline. Both button variants and header controls are 48px. Sort options grow from 40px to 48px on coarse pointers; filter options and reset controls grow from 32px to 48px. Active-filter chips keep their 32px visible box and expand their hit area through a pseudo-element. See Control heights follow the grid for component-specific dimensions.

rules.name: The Swell Rule
rules.body: Each wave line is four components, and the two carrying most of its height travel in opposite directions at almost the same wavelength, so they beat and crests build and dissolve in place rather than marching across. Measured: amplitude breathing alone was invisible at 0.2px/s, a single travelling wave was 83% pure translation and read as a sliding picture, the counter-travelling pair is 70% shape change. The pair is unequal, 0.46 to 0.32, so it calms without ever going flat. Weights stay small because four waves can align where two could not, and the band clipped its canvas at the 78px minimum of --sea-h; any weight change must be checked at every height the clamp produces. Runs at 30fps, draws only while on screen, stops on tab hide, still under reduced motion, and canvas sizing is split from drawing so the loop never reallocates a backing store.

rules.name: The Borrowed Type Rule
rules.body: A social card is the only surface that cannot use the site's own typeface: Iowan Old Style is a macOS system font with no file to embed. Vollkorn stands in, as the closest embeddable face measured against Iowan (x-height over cap +0.010, the width of Hamburgefonstiv within 0.1% at 100px) and the only close match shipping the 500 and 600 weights this scale uses; Inter stands in for -apple-system. Both are SIL OFL 1.1 and carry their licence in the package, which is the standing condition for any font entering this repository. Nothing else on the site may substitute a typeface, and a card never truncates a title: the type steps down the scale instead.

rules.name: The Two Digit Issue Rule
rules.body: An issue number is recorded three digits wide and published two: Issue 08, never Issue 008, and three digits only once there is a hundredth issue. src/data/issue.ts is the single place that produces the label (issueLabel for the digits, issueName for the whole phrase) and scripts/check-editorial-style.mjs fails the build on a literal three-digit form. Both exist because the rule was written down nowhere until 2026-09-03: it had been implemented three times over and skipped in five more places, so the breadcrumb printed Issue 008 directly above a heading reading Issue 08.

rules.name: The Earned Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion is rationed by purpose, not by count. A surface may carry one moving thing or several; what disqualifies any of them is moving without a job. Motion earns its place when it acknowledges an action, makes a state change or spatial relationship legible, preserves continuity through a change, or marks a moment the surface has genuinely earned. Movement that does none of those is animation debt however small, and one decorative flourish is worse than three devices that each explain something. Two obligations follow: every animation needs a prefers-reduced-motion path that reduces movement without erasing meaning, and anything that loops stops while it is off screen. Until 2026-09-03 this was a count, with a third motion forbidden outright; that was arbitrary, permitting a decorative third and forbidding a fourth that explained something.

rules.name: The Pilot Rule
rules.body: The archive's beacon marks which stop the reader is at. One lit dot rests inside a ring and, when the nearest stop changes, makes a single bounded 420ms move to the new one on ease-settle, then rests again. Confined to /archive/. An earlier version followed the scroll position every frame, so it moved the whole time the reader did and travelled faster the harder they scrolled; the state it represents is discrete, and once the dot belonged to a ring rather than to the scroll it held, arrived and stopped responding to scroll speed without any of that being tuned. Scroll decides only which stop is current and CSS owns the movement, so nothing runs on a still page. The fill is a state, so it takes the accent under The Beacon Rule and no stop stays lit behind it. Under prefers-reduced-motion the marker stays and only the travel is dropped.

rules.name: The Landfall Ping
rules.body: Reaching the archive's terminus is the one completion that page has, so the origin answers it with the same three-pulse beacon-ping the RSS mark uses on the subscribe card, on the same keyframes and curve. It fires on arrival rather than on load, because landing is the moment; it is three pulses rather than a loop so it cannot become friction on the way back down; and it re-arms after the reader leaves so returning is acknowledged again. Reduced motion drops it entirely: it carries feeling, not state.

dos: Do keep the fog-grey field, white paper, deep-sea text, and blue accent in a tight relationship.
Do assign prose, chip labels and metadata through --body-text, --chip-text and --muted by meaning rather than by page.
Do reuse the shared page shell so archive, tag, collection, about, and app pages line up.
Do keep shadows soft and ambient.
Do let serif headlines carry the editorial voice while system sans handles utility.
Do keep the defining tag or collection locked when it is the page’s own context.

Do keep the uppercase eyebrow above section and card headings. General design guidance treats a kicker above a heading as filler; here it is load-bearing house style, it names the issue section, the pick and the current-issue block, and it is the documented Label role. This is a deliberate, standing exception.
donts: Don't introduce loud secondary colors just to add energy.
Don't reintroduce warm sand or cream into the light theme; the day palette is white and Deep-Sea-tinted grey.
Don't replace the soft shadow system with hard offsets or heavy glow.
Don't use neutral gray on colored surfaces; derive secondary ink from the surface hue and give each reading role one semantic token.
Don't make chips, filters, or buttons feel like separate UI worlds.
Don't let the brand wordmark typography spread into body copy.
Don't use em dashes or en dashes in public editorial copy.
Don't let the Editor's Pick accent leave that one card, or reach a link, control or state. It is light, not a second accent.
Don't hand-write an iconAccent. Generate it so every pick lands in the same lightness and chroma band.
Don't fill a control with the accent. The dark theme's blue is a foreground colour; as a ground it fails contrast and becomes the brightest thing on the page.
Don't set a local eyebrow gap. Use --eyebrow-gap so every labelled block on the site is bound the same way.
Don't align cards with per-region min-heights. They are guesses, and content that outgrows one knocks its whole row out of step.
Don't apply saturate() to a whole card to knock back its icon. It drains the card's own surface and takes it off the palette's hue.
Don't derive an app's fallback icon or colour in a component. Both come from src/data/app-icon.ts, or the surfaces drift apart.
Don't hard-code an overlay scrim. It is --scrim, and a dark scrim over a light page reads as a dimmed screen rather than frosted glass.
Don't ship a tap target at the height of its text. A nav link is a target, not prose.
Don't swing an ambient animation either side of its still state without checking the still state was not already at the edge of its canvas.
Don't add a font to this repository without its licence file.
